children: rallied on Tuesday after showing that its sales momentum is slowly building.

"This marked our second consecutive quarter of overall revenue growth, with total revenue up 1.1% versus the prior year. The underlying health of our business continued to strengthen across our direct channels, margin structure, and balance sheet," highlighted CEO Ian Brickley.

Direct segment revenues rose 8.0% in Q2 to total $65.4M. Comparable sales increased 9.2%, with all channels positive, driven by improved e-commerce conversion and improved average transaction value across direct channels. Total sales were only up 1.0% to $71.6M but topped the consensus expectation by $5.7M.

Indirect segment revenue was down 39.4% to $6.3M, driven by strategic shifts and timing related to the company's marketplace strategy, in addition to a reduction in liquidation sales, while continued improvements in specialty and department stores partially offset the decline.

Consolidated gross profit was 59.8% of net revenue, compared to 50.1% a year ago. The increase in year-over-year margin rate is primarily due to the impact of $7.7 million for tariff refunds received during the quarter relating to prior period customs entries.
On the balance sheet, Vera Bradley

reported a cash position of $34.2M on August 1 vs. $15.2M at the end of last year’s second quarter and $15.7M at the fiscal year end in January. Notably, the company had no borrowings on its asset-based lending facility during the quarter.
